title: Death Has Been Here, and Borne Away
description: Death Has Been Here, and Borne Away in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 760 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the Boston S. S. H. Book.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Death has been here, and borne a-way A bro-ther from our side: Just in the morn-ing of his day, As young as we he died.

lines: Death has been here, and borne away
Just in the morning of his day,
As young as we he died.
We cannot tell who next may fall
One must be first, but let us all
May each attend with willing feet
And wait around thy mercy seat,
With hope as well as fear.
Lord, to thy wisdom and thy care
Content to live and serve thee here,
Or die and sing thy praise.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
